clue.text: Twisting arm, student changed to another form

indicators.note: twisting something bends it out of its original shape, so the words that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student wrestler gets an arm twisted and comes out a different person.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmute something is to alter its nature or substance, as alchemists hoped to turn lead into gold.

clue.text: Anguish when ex-President shortly gains lead in America

indicators.note: the shortened name gains a letter by taking it inside itself
shortly asks for the name to be cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Harry S Truman, US President 1945 to 1953

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of America is wanted

parts.note: first letter of America

explanation.surface: A former president is in torment after a rival takes the lead in an American election.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortly means only the last letter goes, and the single letter from America is slipped in after the second letter of the shortened name.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is deep emotional shock or distress, a close synonym of great mental suffering.

clue.text: Compounds using English to replace old passages

indicators.note: using brings in a letter to be put into the word for compounds
to replace says the incoming letter takes the place of another one

parts.note: alloys are metallic compounds, mixtures of metals

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: compounds made with English materials take over from old ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using English to replace old' puts E where the O stands in ALLOYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleys are narrow passages or lanes running between buildings.

clue.text: In auditorium, performer serves Heather cocktail

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a performer might be a singer, and to serve a drink is to pour it
ling is another name for heather; with the S that ends the sound above it reads as written

explanation.surface: At a concert hall a performer hands a cocktail to someone called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, singer pours sounds like the city SINGAPORE; ling (heather) completes SLING once the S ends the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Singapore Sling is a well-known gin-based mixed drink created at Raffles Hotel.

clue.text: Find empty library weird

parts.note: to unearth is to dig up or discover

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving just its outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of library

explanation.surface: Discovering an abandoned library feels spooky.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearthly means strange or supernatural, as if not of this world, so eerie or uncanny.

clue.text: Not wholly adored, leafy climbing plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, that is backwards
not wholly means only part of the words is used, so the letters sit inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of adored and the start of leafy

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly admires a leafy climbing plant on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a shrub or small tree bearing white flowers and dark berries.

clue.text: Resent crossing this body of water and we find someone to give answers

definitions.note: a pond is a small body of still water; 'this' points at the answer itself

indicators.note: crossing says the letters of 'Resent' straddle the answer, so taking them away from the longer word leaves it

parts.note: a respondent is a person who answers, as in a survey or a lawsuit
the word resent, its letters split around the answer

explanation.surface: An odd instruction: wrap one word round the answer and you get a person who replies.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: 'Resent crossing' the answer, RES + it + ENT, spells RESPONDENT, someone to give answers, so stripping the letters of RESENT from that word leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond is a small pool of standing water, i.e. a modest lake.

clue.text: Upset about revolution

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in a row over money
a turn is one revolution

explanation.surface: Someone is upset about a political revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to tip over or knock down, as you would upset a glass.

clue.text: Publish record on waste

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
to waste an opportunity is to lose it

explanation.surface: A newspaper decides to print the record about government waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to make information known, revealing it to the public.

clue.text: A menu: chips with cold processed ham

definitions.note: ham used as an adjective, as in a ham actor

indicators.note: processed food has been broken down and reformed, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cafe menu offering chips with cold processed ham.
explanation.walkthrough: Processed ham reads as food, but ham is the definition: a ham actor is an unskilled one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham describes an amateurish, unskilled performance, and someone unaccomplished lacks skill or polish.

clue.text: Stripping job, nothing excluded

indicators.note: stripping means peeling off the outside, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a calling is a vocation or job

explanation.surface: A striptease artist's work, in which nothing is left on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripping job' suggests a striptease, but 'Stripping' takes the outer letters off a word for job.
explanation.definitionFit: All in means inclusive, with every extra counted in the price.

clue.text: Hazards close by French city

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece sits next to the other

parts.note: the close of something is its end
Angers is a city in western France on the Maine

explanation.surface: A list of dangers lying close to a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Here hazards is a verb: to endanger something is to put it at risk.

clue.text: Root around area in wood, part of London

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so read backwards

parts.note: a yam is an edible root vegetable

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: fir is a softwood timber
standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone rummages around a patch of woodland in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Root looks like a verb for digging about, but it is the vegetable, which turns round to give MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayfair is an affluent district of central London's West End, famed for expensive property.

clue.text: Public show using most of land on playing field

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped
in an across clue, placed on means following after the other piece

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a British public sports field
a land is a country, here Italy

explanation.surface: A public event held on most of a sports field.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a performance of music or poetry given before an audience.

clue.text: Male enters carrying spare IT equipment

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: standard abbreviation for male
to board a ship or train is to enter it
a spare one is the other one, the extra

explanation.surface: A man walks in carrying spare computer parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The spare word goes inside M plus BOARDS, between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherboards are the main circuit boards inside computers, so they are hardware for IT.

clue.text: Startled about reversal of evil being reprimanded

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to be rocked is to be shaken or startled

indicators.note: reversal of says the following word is read backwards

parts.note: ill can mean evil, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: Someone shocked by evil being reversed, while getting told off.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone a rollicking is British slang for a severe telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollicked is informal British for scolded or told off severely, so rebuked.

clue.text: Was keen eccentric then exploited?

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the word after it is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
to exploit someone is to use them

explanation.surface: Was the keen oddball then taken advantage of?
explanation.definitionFit: To have enthused is to have shown eager excitement, so to have been keen.

clue.text: Renown of good bread from two foreign areas

parts.note: standard abbreviation for good
bread is slang for money: the rand of South Africa and EUR, the code for the euro

explanation.surface: A baker earns fame for fine bread made with flour from two countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is splendour and greatness, which brings prestige and high standing.

clue.text: Where to see people training with runners?

definitions.text: Where to see people training with runners?

parts.words: Where to see people training with runners?
parts.note: surface: a track where athletes train alongside sprinters; setter's reading: runners are skis, and the training is for beginner skiers on a gentle slope

explanation.walkthrough: Runners suggests athletes, but skis and sledges run too; the place is the gentle slope where learners practise.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery slope is the easy, gentle hill at a ski resort used by beginners learning to ski.

clue.text: Finally time to support burdened fellow

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: Atlas, the Titan in Greek myth, bore the heavens on his shoulders
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Eventually it is time to help a weighed-down man.
explanation.definitionFit: At last means in the end, after a long wait, so eventually.

clue.text: Retrieve mug hiding cache regularly

indicators.note: hiding means concealing inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a mug is a fool, as is an ass

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of cache

explanation.surface: Someone recovers a mug that was hidden in a stash.
explanation.definitionFit: To access data is to obtain or fetch it from storage, as on a computer.

clue.text: Names bore penning new article for Marie Claire

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: bore as the past of bear, as in bore a child: had
standard abbreviation for new
Marie Claire is a French name, and les is a French definite article

explanation.surface: Tedious names are written into a fresh article for a fashion magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Claire looks like the magazine but stands for French.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a person's name or nickname, as on CB radio or online.

clue.text: Kingdom investing billion in source of oil

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: the shea tree yields shea butter, a vegetable oil
standard abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: A kingdom puts a billion into its oil field.
explanation.walkthrough: Source of oil suggests a well or field, but here it is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheba was the ancient kingdom of the biblical Queen of Sheba, in southern Arabia.

clue.text: Stupid kids hid notice: Avoid all edges

indicators.note: avoiding the edges means leaving off each word's first and last letters

parts.note: kids without its outside letters
hid without its outside letters
notice without its outside letters

explanation.surface: Silly children hid a notice warning them to keep away from the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means foolish or senseless, a direct synonym.

clue.text: This writer if poorly might get sick benefit

definitions.note: an American novelist, author of The Grapes of Wrath

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters of 'sick benefit' are in a bad way and must be rearranged
might get says what the rearranged fodder could turn into, the answer together with the extra word

explanation.surface: An author, if he fell ill, might be able to claim state sickness pay.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: the answer plus IF together use exactly the letters of SICK BENEFIT, which 'poorly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck was the American novelist who wrote Of Mice and Men, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Strained fling's great pleasure cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the end is lopped off, dropping the final letter

parts.note: heaven is bliss or great delight

explanation.surface: A tense holiday romance brings joy that ends too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: Fling suggests a brief affair, but here it is a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A heave is an effortful throw, hurling something heavy with great exertion.

clue.text: Fish out of water gains nothing

indicators.note: gains means takes in, so a letter is added inside

parts.note: something out of the water is dry
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A fish out of water gets nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish out of water reads as the idiom, but fish is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The dory, or John Dory, is a flat-bodied sea fish prized as food.

clue.text: Preserve with fruit covering papers for applicants

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: dates are fruit of the date palm
identity papers, ID for short

explanation.surface: Jam and fruit are wrapped in paper for job seekers.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates are people who apply for a job or stand for election.
